answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprinting Rule. Each agent identity is fingerprinted by its task-type mix, latency profile, and interaction graph across epochs; a new identity inherits a copper baseline only after reproducing the prior epoch's fingerprint within tolerance. Identities whose behaviour diverges from their orchard of historical traces get throttled and must re-earn throughput through sustained consistency. Sybils splitting into fresh identities start hollow, with no history to match, so each one must pay full ramp-up compute and latency cost before reaching useful capacity.
